items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Now Pete could tell you, yeah, he could tell you just who was playing out there.

ctx.x: I just remember who was playing with him. I don't know who had the band, did you hear? No, I don't remember all that.

Now Pete could tell you, yeah, he could tell you just who was playing out there. But he used to lay off from there on Sunday night, Saturday, Sunday, or Monday night, and play with Ory. See, he played with that band and played with Ory's band at that time, and I knew of him, you know, see. That was around 1917, 1918. Frankie Dewson played out there a good while, and I don't know whether he was playing with Frankie Dewson or not. See, he could have been. Frankie played with the manager of the band out there.
It must have been the Eagle or something.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: See, he quit the band with P. the book out there.

ctx.x: No, I mean, in 32 or so.

Oh, he broke up with P. the book out there. Yeah. He just quit the band. See, he quit the band with P. the book out there. Then he made up this band. See, he consists of me, Eddie Pearson, Leo Desjard, Joe Phillips, Arthur Durbney, Elliot Taylor, Manuel Sayles, and Simon Moreira. And a singer by the name of Harold Wells. That was his band. And we played together from 32 until 35. I did.
And I left the band in 35.

items.title: Bob Watts Interview, 1963-02-28
items.q: And I mean, them guys couldn't play. Peter Hunter, I told you.

ctx.x: And Jimmy John, Simon was on bass. It's time to take him sick. Then we got a guy out of St. Louis, Jimmy, Jimmy Jones. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. And I mean, them guys couldn't play. Peter Hunter, I told you. You know what happened? Set them David Horn on the left. He stayed out in the hour. Yeah.
He went on to say, huh?
